subject: Runway leadership sync: capacity scenarios & GPU unit economics
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Subject: Runway leadership sync: capacity scenarios & GPU unit economics

Team —

QBR prep note: we need a concise leadership-ready slice on capacity runway and unit economics for infra (GPU spend, utilization, and the impact of batching/caching) by next week. I attached a modeling workbook (runway_modeling_v3.xlsx) and a short experiment summary; please review and push back with numbers or concerns.

Context / ask:
- QBR is scheduled for Tue 12/14; slide deck due Fri 12/11 COB.
- Goal: present a defensible 3-month runway and two mitigations that buy us runway with minimal customer impact.

Baseline scenarios in the workbook (please verify / update):
1) "Steady" — traffic flat, utilization ~current; 3-month spend projection included.
2) "+20% organic" — typical seasonal uplift; focus on autoscale and preemptible bursts.
3) "Holiday burst" — +60% token volume for short window; test canary roll for priority routes.

Specific data I need from each of you by Wed 12/09 EOD:
- Aditya: updated live GPU pool counts, 7/30/90-day utilization, p95 latency and p50 token-cost numbers under current batching.
- Irene: any security/compliance constraints that would change caching or batching for Private/Dedicated customers (e.g., KMS, cache encryption, PII redaction).
- Lauren: leadership asks / tradeoffs you want surfaced (SLA vs cost vs feature gating).
- Mina: ask finance to sketch quick 3-month spend curve (conservative / likely / optimistic) and attach to the workbook.

Proposed mitigations to quantify (feel free to add):
- Increase batch size profile for non-interactive routes (reduce per-token GPU cycles).
- Prefix / KV caching on common prompts + TTL tuning (target 25–35% aggregate token reduction in best-effort workloads).
- Burst priority lanes for Dedicated customers (cost pass-through model).

Notes on measurement: include expected latency delta (p50/p95), expected unit cost delta ($/token or $/GPU-hour), and rollback plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

Attachments referenced: runway_modeling_v3.xlsx, batching-experiments-summary.pdf, qbr-agenda-draft.md

Thanks — I want this framed for an exec audience: clear decision ask, tradeoffs, and numbers.

— Jonas

Jonas / Lauren — quick numbers from infra telemetry and the experiments repo (see batching-experiments-summary.pdf):

Current fleet snapshot (live):
- GPU types: 84x A100-40GB + 36x A100-80GB (total 120 GPUs).
- Average utilization (30d): 62%. 7d: 68% (weekend dip).
- p95 latency on >512-token routes: 220 ms; p50: 90 ms.

Unit economics — hosted generation routes (current batching):
- Measured infra cost: ~$0.00090 per token (includes GPU amortization + infra overhead).
- Effective token count after existing caching: ~8% reduction on baseline traffic.

Experiment highlights (from internal A/B):
- Increasing batch size for long-running routes (batch factor +25%) => ~18% reduction in GPU cycles per token; p95 latency increases ~12% (from 220 ms to ~246 ms) on that route class.
- KV/prefix caching on standardized prompts => 12–15% end-to-end token reduction in mixed workloads. Hit-rate varies by customer; target optimization: 20–30% hit rate on templated app traffic.

Risk and suggested guardrails:
- Canary plan: new batch profile to 10% traffic for 48h, monitor p95 and error rates; auto-roll back below threshold.
- Cost modeling: if we hit +20% traffic with current stack we need +24 GPUs sustained (A100-40GB equiv) to maintain p95 SLA — or ~2.6x efficiency improvement from batching/caching to avoid hardware add.

I'll upload a compact csv with utilization slices to the Drive link and annotate the workbook.

- Aditya

Folks — quick compliance checklist to keep in mind if we push caching / TTL increases: 

- Private/Dedicated customers: many have strict requirements on cached data and KMS. We must:
  - Offer an opt-out for KV/prefix caching at tenant level.
  - Ensure cache encryption keys are customer-specific where required (HSM/KMS).
  - Redaction: we should not cache tokens containing PII; add a redaction pipeline before writing to KV cache.

- Audit & evidence: SOC2 sprints will need docs showing: cache policies, TTLs, key management, and redaction tests. This adds ~2–3 weeks of compliance work for Private customers if they request tenant-specific controls.

Operational suggestion: implement a "compliance-safe" cache profile (default for Dedicated) with TTL=0 until consent/configured; allow hosted customers to use aggressive TTLs.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance

Subject: Runway: decisions & next steps (summary)

Thanks all for the quick turn. Consolidated decisions for the QBR slide and follow-ups: 

Decisions (leadership-ready):
1) Run two prioritized experiments this week:
   - Batch profile bump for non-interactive generation routes (canary to 10% traffic, metric gates p95<260ms, error rate unchanged).
   - Aggressive prefix/KV cache profile for hosted routes with TTL=2h and conservative TTL for Dedicated (opt-in).
2) Canary plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with automated rollback rules. Dry-run of canary monitoring dashboard: Mon 12/13 10:00 PT.
3) Finance ask (Mina): produce 3-month spend curves (conservative/likely/optimistic) that include a model for hardware buy vs savings from mitigations.
4) Compliance: Irene will draft a short slide on Dedicated cache controls (KMS, TTL opt-out, redaction) and estimate the extra time if customers request tenant-level keys.

Open items / asks:
- Aditya: please confirm the exact GPU-add counts for +20% and +60% scenarios in the workbook by EOD 12/10 (I know you sent roughs; need final numbers for the deck).
- Lauren: I'll drop a leadership framing slide into qbr-agenda-draft.md; can you review and mark any changes by 12/11 noon?
- Mina: attach finance curves to the workbook and include a short recommendation (buy vs optimize) by COB 12/11.

Attachments: updated agenda draft (qbr-agenda-draft.md) and pointers to the experiment PDF.

I'll compile a one-page executive summary for the deck mid-day tomorrow. If there are any objections to the mitigations above, raise them before the dry-run.

— Jonas
